classification.difficultyReason: Connect the areas of squares on a right triangle to Pythagoras, infer x²+(x+2)²=34, and solve the quadratic while excluding a negative length.

content.prompt:
Three squares surround a right-angled triangle. The shaded square has area of $34\text{ cm}^2$.
What is the value of $x$?

spec.description: Three external squares on the sides of a right-angled triangle. All four dimension labels and the right-angle marker are retained. Only the hypotenuse square is shaded. Drawing proportions do not supply numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: The perpendicular legs have lengths x and x+2. The square on the hypotenuse has area 34 square centimetres, so x²+(x+2)²=34.
spec.answerVisibility: Question geometry and givens only; no solution or numerical value of x.

answer.short: $x=3\text{ cm}$. Use $x^2+(x+2)^2=34$ and retain the positive solution.
answer.worked:
Using Pythagoras:
$$\begin{align*}
x^2+(x+2)^2&=34\\
2x^2+4x-30&=0\\
x^2+2x-15&=0
\end{align*}$$
With $a=1$, $b=2$ and $c=-15$:
$$\begin{align*}
x&=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{2^2-4(1)(-15)}}{2(1)}\\
x&=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{64}}{2}\\
x&=3\text{ or }-5
\end{align*}$$
A length must be positive, so $x=3\text{ cm}$.
